reasons: Section 12.4 bars Customer from acquiring or developing any competing product or service for the full term plus 24 months, in any territory, with no category limit and no performance-based exit — this squarely matches the rule's detection guidance ('shall not procure … from any third party') and sits in walk-away territory, well past the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic exit on Vendor performance failure), so a deviation finding is correct.

The redline reaches the preferred position: the offending covenant is removed and replaced with a non-exclusivity confirmation that imposes no new obligations on Customer and preserves nothing adverse; the failed 'minimal edit' check (0.679 changed-character ratio) is expected for a clause-level deletion/replacement of this kind and is not a substantive defect.

The rationale correctly avoids double-counting: the Section 7.2 disclose-and-match right of first refusal is routed to the MFN rule and Section 2.1's minimum volume to the volume-commitment rule, and it correctly notes the internal contradiction with Section 12.3, which supports deletion rather than narrowing.
The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, cites the preferred position and the supporting Section 12.3, and explains what changed without lecturing.
